seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on the answer below. `answer.txt` holds the same text and I've left the room. I traced the program by hand and did not run it.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

My first trace had 101 where the answer has 100, from the `CALL outer 1` line. Inside `inner`, `a` is `outer`'s local and isn't visible to `inner`, so it reads as the global 0. That gives 0 + 100 = 100.

seats.name: seat-3
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The program prints 35 values, and I wrote them to `answer.txt` on one line:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I traced the program by hand against the spec. I did not run it, since there is no STAMP interpreter here.

Room rq1 concluded 3/3 on this exact text. The only disagreement was the last two values, `CALL outer 1` and `CALL inner 5`. seat-1's opening had 101 for `CALL outer 1`, because `inner` seemed to see outer's parameter `a`. The spec says a call reads only its own locals and then the globals. So `a` reads as 0 inside `inner`, giving 100, and seat-1 conceded. I have left the room.
